title: Two kinds of interface: parity across 2-edge cuts, knot against hub across 3-edge cuts
claim: The knot's spaces have two kinds of interface. Let H be a knot's space (connected cubic system on which not-all-equal fails) and consider a nontrivial cut of its incidence graph (two shores of more than one vertex, every removed edge joining them). (1) Balance: 3(p - l) = a - b gives, for 2 edges, one port and one slot on each shore, and for 3 edges a point side with all three ports and a line side with all three slots. (2) Across every nontrivial 2-edge cut one shore accepts exactly equality and the other exactly disequality on the two channels (non-empty, disjoint, complement-closed), so the shores meet as complementary two-place parity and neither acts as a hub. (3) Across every nontrivial 3-edge cut the point side accepts exactly one antipodal pair {v, v-bar} and the line side exactly its complement (the atom lemma excludes four-state sides and two two-state sides; a signed point closing the line side, with the signed Seymour bound, excludes a two-state line side); exchanging colours on the channels where v is 1 gives equality (a hub) against not-all-equal (the knot). This corrects KNOT-COMPOSE-20261101-001A: its 'compose only through hubs' (Theorem 4(3)) fails wherever a knot's space has a nontrivial 2-edge cut (odd cycles of Fano blocks, the twisted cube, splices containing them), and its 'exactly equality and not-all-equal' (Theorem 4(1)) holds only up to that exchange; its statement that hub-free failure is parity stands. Computed on ten knot's spaces: 40 nontrivial 2-edge cuts (none in splice trees, k(k-1)/2 in a cycle of k blocks, 3 in the twisted cube) and 48 nontrivial 3-edge cuts in five spaces (21 twisted, all in cyclic spaces).
failure_conditions: A nontrivial 2-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph with unbalanced sides.
A nontrivial 2-edge cut of a knot's space whose sides are not equality and disequality.
A nontrivial 3-edge cut of a knot's space whose point side is not one antipodal pair or whose line side is not its complement.
foundation_claim_scope: A structural theorem on the interfaces of the knot's spaces; no counting claim.
